subject: Recap & next steps — KMS/HSM options for FinBank pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@finbank.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finbank.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — KMS/HSM options for FinBank pilot

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thorough walkthrough of FinBank's security constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we maintain momentum: 

Call highlights:
- FinBank requirement: customer control over root key material and proof of non-exportability for production keys.
- Data residency: primary workload must remain in eu-west-1; logs related to production inference cannot be routed outside the region.
- Audit/logging: full per-request audit trail required for at least 24 months; token-level payloads should be pseudonymized for analytics.
- Rotation: preference for hardware-backed rotation and documented KMS rotation processes.

Proposed options (high-level) — see attached 'redwood-kms-options-v1.pdf' for a short comparison table:
1) Managed Redwood KMS (not preferred): easiest path, Redwood manages keys and rotation. Does not meet non-exportability requirement.
2) BYOK with cloud provider KMS + HSM root: we can integrate with AWS KMS where FinBank controls a CMK that we never export. For an HSM-rooted workflow, CloudHSM or KMS with imported key material (via HSM) is an option — we outlined steps and caveats in the attached checklist.
3) Private deployment: deploy Redwood Private in your VPC (or on-prem) with direct HSM connection. Gives greatest control and separation; tradeoffs are increased ops and longer lead time.

Immediate asks from our side to scope an accurate SOW and timeline: 
- Confirm whether FinBank will accept AWS CloudHSM-backed keys, Azure Key Vault HSM, or requires on-prem HSM appliances.
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency for pilot (we need realistic token/sec + average seq lengths).
- Desired log retention window and whether pseudonymized analytics (no raw token storage) is acceptable for business monitoring.
- Procurement timeline & security questionnaire owner — we should also send SOC2 evidence (attached).

Next steps: 
- Camila (cc'd) will draft a short technical comparison and show a mapping to Redwood integration steps.
- If BYOK is acceptable, we can prepare an integration checklist and initial SOW draft (target: 1 week).

I'll follow up with a one-pager and the integration checklist attached. Let me know if I've omitted anything important.

Thanks,
Jonas
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-kms-options-v1.pdf
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@finbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finbank.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — KMS/HSM options for FinBank pilot

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our security team after the call: 

- FinBank's policy: production keys must be stored in customer-controlled HSMs where key material is non-exportable. We can provision CloudHSM instances in AWS eu-west-1, or we can provide on-prem HSM appliances. Azure Key Vault HSM is also supported but we'd need proof of FIPS 140-2 Level 3 equivalence.
- Logs: we cannot ship raw request payloads off-region. You can ship pseudonymized metrics (request hashes, token counts, latency) to Redwood for monitoring. Audit logs (access events, key usage) must be retained for 24 months and stored in our S3 in eu-west-1.
- Rotation: we expect a hardware-backed rotation process (annual rotation acceptable) and documentation for re-wrapping historical content where needed.
- Timeline: procurement can be accelerated if we have a SOW + T&Cs within 5 business days. Security questionnaire (attached via the portal) will go to your compliance team.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports key wrapping so that you never have access to the plaintext root key? Also need to understand whether Redwood's telemetry can be configured to exclude PII and raw prompts.

Thanks,
Rebecca
Head of Cloud Security — FinBank

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@finbank.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — KMS/HSM options for FinBank pilot

Hi Rebecca — thanks for the specifics, that makes scoping much clearer. Below is a technical digest mapping FinBank's constraints to three concrete integration patterns and the immediate gaps to resolve. I'm happy to jump on a short tech call to walk through diagrams.

Option A — Customer KMS (preferred balance of control + hosted):
- Flow: FinBank creates a customer-managed KMS CMK in eu-west-1. Redwood performs envelope encryption: we generate per-model data keys, encrypt them with the customer CMK (AWS KMS Encrypt API) and never persist the unencrypted customer key.
- HSM requirement: If you require a hardware root, CloudHSM-backed CMKs are possible; we will need CloudHSM cluster access patterns and key policy review (attachment: cloudhsm-integration-checklist.xlsx).
- Logs & residency: Audit events (KMS Decrypt calls, key rotation events) can be logged to FinBank's CloudTrail/S3 bucket in eu-west-1. Application-level telemetry can be pseudonymized before Redwood aggregates it.
- Pros: meets non-exportability; short deployment timeline (we can integrate in 2–4 weeks for a pilot).
- Cons: requires FinBank to provision KMS/CloudHSM and share access patterns/policies for validation.

Option B — Private deployment inside your VPC with HSM tunnel:
- Flow: Deploy Redwood Private into your VPC; connect to on-prem or cloud HSM via dedicated network link. Keys never leave your environment.
- Pros: maximum control and separation; easier for auditors.
- Cons: longer lead time (4–10 weeks), higher ops footprint and higher cost.

Option C — Hosted with Redwood-managed HSM (only if policy allows):
- Flow: Redwood holds HSM-backed keys; we can provide contractual and technical controls, but this does not satisfy non-exportability requirements.

Key rotation and re-wrap: we support both automated KMS rotation workflows and manual re-wrap scripts. For BYOK flows we support re-encryption/rewrap of persisted model caches and KV stores; rewrap may have a short maintenance window depending on dataset size.

Telemetry and PII: Redwood can configure ingestion rules to strip raw prompts and tokens, keeping only hashes and aggregate metrics for analytics. We recommend a staged telemetry plan: pilot with pseudonymized telemetry → evaluate completeness → expand as needed.

Deliverables we propose this week: 
- Draft SOW for a BYOK pilot (if CloudHSM/AKV-HSM acceptable) including scoping QPS, retention SLAs, and migration plan.
- Integration checklist (attached) and a SOC2 evidence bundle: soc2-srt-evidence.zip.
- Proposed pilot schedule: kickoff + environment prep (week 1), integrate KMS/HSM + smoke tests (week 2), pilot run (weeks 3–4).

Please confirm which HSM providers (CloudHSM, Azure KV HSM, or on-prem vendor) you'd like us to include in the SOW. If acceptable, we'll prepare a one-page SOW and an initial cost estimate.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cloudhsm-integration-checklist.xlsx, soc2-srt-evidence.zip
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@finbank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finbank.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — KMS/HSM options for FinBank pilot

Thanks Camila — that aligns with our expectations. Two quick asks before procurement: 
1) Please include Azure Key Vault HSM in the SOW options (we use multi-cloud HSM for redundancy).
2) Can you produce a 1-page SOW and a security addendum that explicitly states: keys are customer-managed, Redwood has no access to plaintext root key, audit logs remain in eu-west-1 S3 owned by FinBank?

If you can send those by EOD Friday we can prioritize internal approvals and aim to sign a pilot SOW next week. Also schedule a 30-minute follow-up tech review for Thursday (Tom will send a calendar invite).

Best,
Rebecca
Head of Cloud Security — FinBank
